description: This is a team entirely made up of high school students so far, we intend to make an app which will assist the upcoming Artemis mission in landing safely on the moon by finding the safest lunar landing locations available.
summary: There are a lot of factors that go into deciding where exactly to land a spaceship, rover, or other piece or machinery during a space mission, so this app quickly combines them all. It takes documented mission records and terrain measurements of lunar landing sites; finding users the most suitable lunar landing site tailored to the mission's priorities and compares 20 different landing sites based on how well they meet the needs of the mission. Every location is ranked on slope of terrain, communication with Earth, sunlight availability, and proximity to ice, users are also prompted to select a type of rocket since different rockets handle slope differently. Typically, mission coordinators have to calculate and compare this data across many different platforms, but our app holds all the information in one spot and can hopefully save time when planning out a space expedition to the Moon.
details: This website analyzes and utilizes lunar data to perform calculations that help determine the best landing site for a mission. It works by gathering data from NASA databases and analyzing it through a pre-programmed process to recommend and visualize the most suitable landing locations based on the user's mission requirements. This benefits future space exploration by simplifying the process of finding safe and efficient landing locations, reducing the time needed to compare potential sites, and providing users with multiple choices through a visually appealing and easy-to-navigate webpage. The intended impact of this project is to support future lunar exploration by helping scientists and space agencies identify safer, more efficient, and scientifically valuable landing locations, particularly for upcoming Artemis missions. This project was developed using HTML, CSS, JSON, and JavaScript to create the website, process lunar data, perform weighted calculations, and display interactive visualizations. We also incorporated NASA lunar imagery and terrain data to make the experience more realistic and informative. Our project is creative because it combines scientific data, customizable mission priorities, rocket compatibility requirements, and an interactive lunar map into one platform. Rather than simply displaying possible landing sites, it allows users to adjust the importance of different factors and receive recommendations tailored to their mission. Some of the most important factors our team considered were astronaut safety, terrain slope, sunlight availability for solar power, communication with Earth, and proximity to water ice. We also considered the different requirements of crewed and robotic missions, since each has different limitations and priorities. By combining these factors into a weighted scoring system, our project provides an accessible and practical tool for comparing lunar landing locations and helping prepare for the future of space exploration.
